## County to talk grant for American Eagle distribution center

Published 2:00 am Sunday, September 6, 2026

 By Dean Stephens 

| Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... |
| --- |

At their Sept. 8 meeting, Rowan County commissioners will decide the fate of a grant related to a major clothing apparel company coming to Salisbury. Commissioners will decide whether or not to be the administrators of an One NC Grant totaling $150,000. The grant funds are earmarked for a new American Eagle Outfitters distribution hub.

Grant proceeds are designated for “installation or purchase of equipment; structural repairs, improvements or renovations to existing buildings to be used for expansions; construction of or improvements to new or existing water, sewer, gas or electric utility distribution lines or equipment for existing buildings, or few new or proposed buildings to be used for manufacturing and industrial operations,” according to One NC grant terms.

The proposed facility is planned for 1415 Peeler Road. The deal could result in at least 63 new full-time positions, according to county staff.

en.Wedoany.com Reported - A.P. Moeller Maersk announced an expansion in the Boston area, planning to open a new distribution center in Hopedale, Mass., by the end of August. # Indiana Packers marks opening of Delphi distribution center

 Tuesday, August 18, 2026 05:42 PM EDT By Alex Brown 

(Photo courtesy of Indiana Packers Corp.)

Delphi-based Indiana Packers Corp. has cut the ribbon on its new distribution center that it says more than doubles its warehouse capacity.

The new facility will bring 30 new jobs to the company’s Carroll County operation, which already employs more than 2,000 people.

“This new facility reinforces our long-term commitment to our team members, producers, customers, Carroll County, Delphi, and the northcentral Indiana community,” Indiana Packers President and Chief Operating Officer Eric Sheiss said in written remarks.

The facility, which some reports say is the result of a $44 million investment, adds more than 96,000 square feet of new freezer space for the company and increases its frozen pallet storage capacity by more than 12 times.

The company said the facility will allow it to provide faster and more efficient shipping to customers across the United States and in more than 20 other countries.

 Aug 5, 2026 | 4:43 PM 

SANFORD, N.C. (WPTF) — A leading health care company, will create 335 jobs in Lee County. The company will invest $600 million in a new manufacturing and distribution center in the city of Sanford.

“STERIS is making a major investment in North Carolina, which reinforces our state’s reputation as a powerhouse in the life sciences industry,” said Governor Josh Stein. “Decades of excellence in manufacturing and innovation have developed the world-class talent, research, and supply chain that continues to attract global companies and drive long-term economic growth across our state.”

Founded in 1985, STERIS is a global provider of products and services that support patient care with an emphasis on infection prevention. STERIS employs more than 18,000 people across approximately 250 locations in more than 35 countries. # Nestle Purina Petcare Factory officially opens in Clermont County

Updated: 10:45 AM EDT Sep 2, 2026

Updated: 10:45 AM EDT Sep 2, 2026

CINCINNATI —

The newest Nestle Purina Petcare Factory opened its doors on Monday, bringing hundreds of new jobs and investments in southwest Ohio.

The plant, which opened on State Route 32 in Batavia, is aimed at helping families and their pets for generations to come.

“As of today, we've generated over 430 new jobs, and we're going to continue to bring the factory to life,” factory manager Mike Ferrito said. “We're just getting started now. Over the next year, we'll continue to bring operations to life and hire over 500 people.”

Purina leaders, local and state officials, and community partners came together to celebrate the company’s 24 th factory in the United States, and the company’s first ground-up factory construction in more than 50 years.

Brian Baldridge, the director of the Ohio Department of Agriculture, said the company is already working with local elevators for the products.
